Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at mostly high settings is comfortably within the Deck's capability for this 2012 title; the 10 W TDP gives the APU room to breathe without draining the battery too fast. Motion blur is disabled to keep the image clean on the small screen.

profiles.Summary: Dishonored is a 2012 immersive-sim with modest PC requirements well below what the Steam Deck can offer, and it runs excellently under Proton with a Platinum rating. The game is lightweight enough to hit 60 fps at native resolution with low TDP, leaving plenty of headroom for battery-friendly play.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the game's 2012 PC minimum/recommended requirements (GTX 460 class) versus the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU (GTX 1050 Ti class), which outclasses those requirements significantly. On your first run, verify that the 60 fps cap holds in dense outdoor areas like Kaldwin's Bridge — if it dips, reduce Shadow Quality to Medium.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with FSR upscaling keeps GPU load very low; the 6 W TDP cap and 800 MHz GPU clock maximize playtime on a single charge. Dishonored's art style holds up well even at reduced resolution.

Older id Tech 4 / Unreal-adjacent engine may occasionally stutter on first shader compile
No native Linux build; runs via Proton but is well-proven at Platinum tier

MaxPerformance.Notes: Maximum GPU clock and full 15 W TDP let the Deck push Dishonored's 2012 engine to its limits at native resolution with all quality settings maxed; the game is old enough that this is comfortably achievable. Expect a stable 60 fps in virtually all areas.

Optimal.Notes: The Deck GPU comfortably exceeds the game's recommended spec, so native 1280x800 at mixed medium/high settings holds a rock-solid 60 fps in virtually all areas. A 9 W TDP cap is enough headroom.
